title: What asbestos training do Australian construction workers and removalists need?
description: Model WHS Regulations asbestos training: r 445 awareness training, r 460 licensed removal worker certification, supervisor requirements and 5 year records.
shortAnswer: Australia's model Work Health and Safety Regulations set three tiers of asbestos training. Regulation 445 requires training in identification, safe handling and control measures for workers who may do asbestos removal or asbestos-related work. Regulation 460 requires licensed removal workers to hold certification in the specified course for their class of work plus job specific training. Licensed removalists' named supervisors need the supervision course and 1 or 3 years' experience. Training records are kept for 5 years.
keyTakeaways: Regulation 445 applies to any worker a business reasonably believes may be involved in asbestos removal work or asbestos-related work, which includes many construction trades who may disturb asbestos during renovation or maintenance.
Removal of 10 square meters or less of non-friable asbestos does not need a license, but regulation 458(3) requires it to be done by a competent person trained under regulation 445.

Licensed removal workers must hold certification in the specified course for Class A (friable) or Class B (non-friable) work, and must receive training specific to each workplace's asbestos removal control plan.
Named supervisors need the specified supervision course, with at least 3 years of relevant industry experience for a Class A license or 1 year for Class B.
Regulation 445 and 461 training records must be kept while the worker does the work and for 5 years after they stop.
jurisdiction: Australia (model WHS laws, adopted in all jurisdictions except Victoria)
regulator: Safe Work Australia (model laws) and state and territory WHS regulators
appliesTo: PCBUs whose workers may be involved in asbestos removal work or asbestos-related work, including builders, plumbers, electricians, carpenters and demolition contractors
Licensed asbestos removalists holding Class A or Class B licenses
Asbestos removal workers and nominated asbestos removal supervisors

sections.heading: What are the tiers of asbestos training under the model WHS Regulations?

blocks.text: There are three: general asbestos training under regulation 445, certified training for licensed removal workers under regulation 460, and certified supervision training for the supervisors named on a removal license. All three sit in Chapter 8 of the [model Work Health and Safety Regulations](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/doc/model-work-health-and-safety-regulations), and they add to the general duty to provide information, training and instruction in Part 3.2.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the model WHS Regulations (December 5, 2025 version) and the model Codes of Practice How to safely remove asbestos and How to manage and control asbestos in the workplace, both amended in November 2026 to move from workplace exposure standards to workplace exposure limits, which take effect December 1, 2026. Status as at November 2026. The model laws operate in every jurisdiction except Victoria, and local regulations may differ in numbering and detail.

sections.heading: Who needs general asbestos training under regulation 445?

blocks.text: Any worker the business reasonably believes may be involved in asbestos removal work or asbestos-related work, other than licensed removal workers covered by regulation 460. Regulation 445(1) requires the person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU) to ensure those workers "are trained in the identification and safe handling of, and suitable control measures for, asbestos and ACM" (asbestos containing material). The maximum penalty is at tier E in the 2025 model text.

The test is reasonable belief about what the worker may encounter, not whether asbestos removal is the worker's job. A plumber, electrician or carpenter working on buildings that may contain asbestos is a typical case. The [model Code of Practice: How to safely remove asbestos](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/doc/model-code-practice-how-safely-remove-asbestos) suggests the training cover:

items: types, uses and likely presence of asbestos in the workplace
roles and responsibilities under the asbestos management plan
where the asbestos register is, how to access it and how to read it
safe work procedures to prevent exposure, including from accidental release
correct use of personal protective equipment, including respiratory protective equipment, where applicable
exposure limits and control levels, and the purpose of any exposure or health monitoring

blocks.text: Regulation 445(3) requires a record of the training to be kept while the worker carries out the work and for 5 years after the day the worker stops working for the PCBU, and 445(4) requires the record to be available for inspection.

sections.heading: What training is needed to remove small amounts of asbestos without a license?

blocks.text: Regulation 445 training. Under regulation 458, a PCBU commissioning removal must use a licensed removalist, except for 10 square meters or less of non-friable asbestos (or associated asbestos contaminated dust), or dust that is only a minor contamination. In those cases regulation 458(3) requires the work to be carried out "by a competent person who has been trained in accordance with regulation 445."

The Code of Practice is specific about what counts: workers carrying out removal that does not require a license must be trained in identification and safe handling first, and "an asbestos awareness course or the non-friable removal unit of competency would be considered appropriate training." The Code gives the example of a plumber removing a small amount of non-friable asbestos during renovation or maintenance.

sections.heading: What training do licensed asbestos removal workers need?

blocks.text: Certification in the specified course for the class of work, and training specific to each job. Regulation 460(1) says a licensed removalist "must not direct or allow a worker to carry out licensed asbestos removal work unless the removalist is satisfied that the worker holds a certification in relation to the specified VET course for asbestos removal relevant to the class of licensed asbestos removal work." The model Regulations name the specified courses as Remove friable asbestos for Class A work and Remove non friable asbestos for Class B work.

Class A covers friable asbestos (regulation 485). Class B covers more than 10 square meters of non-friable asbestos or ACM (regulation 487). The Code says the Class B removal unit must be completed before the Class A unit.

Regulation 460(2) adds "appropriate training", defined in 460(3) as training "designed specifically for the workplace where the licensed asbestos removal work is carried out and the work to be carried out at the workplace." The Code says this should be given before each removal job and should cover the hazards, health effects, the job's asbestos removal control plan, methods and equipment, PPE and RPE, decontamination, waste disposal and emergency procedures. Regulation 461 requires these training records to be kept while the worker does licensed work and for 5 years after they stop, and to be readily accessible at the removal area.

sections.heading: What qualifications must asbestos removal supervisors hold?

blocks.text: Each supervisor named on a removal license must be at least 18, hold certification in the Supervise asbestos removal course and the removal course for the license class, and have relevant industry experience. Regulation 498 sets 3 years of experience for Class A supervisors, and regulation 499 sets 1 year for Class B.

Regulation 459 sets supervision presence. For Class A work the nominated supervisor must be present at the removal area whenever the work is carried out. For Class B work the supervisor must be readily available. The Code gives an example of what that means: contactable by phone and able to arrive at the workplace within 20 minutes. A self-employed person working alone on Class B removal must hold both the worker and supervisor competencies as well as the license.

blocks.text: Work that is likely to disturb asbestos is also high risk construction work under regulation 291(d), so a SWMS is required, as covered on the [SWMS and high risk construction work](/regulations/construction-swms-and-high-risk-construction-work-training) page.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents the asbestos tiers, license classes and roles as a structured framework, and links each role to the knowledge and assessment points its tier requires. When a Code of Practice is amended, as both asbestos Codes were in November 2026, the affected concepts and courses can be traced directly.

faqs.q: Is asbestos awareness training mandatory for all construction workers?
faqs.a: The model Regulations require regulation 445 training for workers the business reasonably believes may be involved in asbestos removal work or asbestos-related work. That is narrower than all workers, but in practice it covers most trades who renovate, maintain or demolish older buildings. The general construction induction course covers common construction hazards, but it is not the specific identification and safe handling training regulation 445 describes.

faqs.q: How long must asbestos training records be kept?
faqs.a: Regulation 445(3) requires records to be kept while the worker carries out the work and for 5 years after the day the worker ceases working for the business. Regulation 461 sets the same 5 year period for licensed removal workers, and requires the record to be readily accessible at the asbestos removal area.

faqs.q: Does an asbestos awareness course allow a worker to remove asbestos?
faqs.a: Only within the unlicensed limit. The Code of Practice says an awareness course or the non-friable removal unit is appropriate training for removing 10 square meters or less of non-friable asbestos. Anything above that, and any friable asbestos, needs a licensed removalist and certified workers.

faqs.q: Are these rules the same in every Australian state?
faqs.a: The model Regulations are adopted in every jurisdiction except Victoria, but each state's own regulation may number provisions differently or add requirements. Victoria regulates asbestos under its own occupational health and safety laws. Check the regulator in the state where the work takes place.
